title: Cross-tenant ingestion watermark inversion causing sporadic metric omissions and trace discontinuities
creator: Asha Menon
description:
Summary: Multiple customers reported intermittent missing timeseries and broken dashboard widgets during a rolling rebalancing event across Dedicated clusters. Investigation shows a rare 'watermark inversion' where ingestion shard watermarks for short-lived tenant shards were rolled back during topology handoff, causing index tombstoning downstream and subsequent trace-span stitcher to drop spans without a backfill.

Symptoms observed: dashboards show gaps for recent 1-10 minute windows; live panels show zeroes then resume; traces missing spans that correspond to same request IDs visible in upstream proxies. Incident correlated with an autoscaler-induced shard move and an ingress retry pattern from a client SDK.

Root cause hypothesis: when a shard reassignment overlaps with an ingestion leader flip, the local shard watermark persisted earlier timestamp due to delayed watermark checkpointing. Downstream index reconciler treats the older watermark as authoritative and issues tombstones for the higher-time series buckets, which removes recently ingested metrics from the queryable index while raw spans remain in object storage—causing trace stitching to fail.

Work done so far: reproduced in staging with a script that forces concurrent leader elections + synthetic retries; added extra logging to shard coordinator and reconciler; implemented a two-step watermark merge that prefers max(watermark, incoming) with idempotent checkpoints; added a compensating backfill job that replays tombstoned buckets when detected.

Planned next steps: land hotfix to reconciler and coordinator (PR linked), run canary on non-customer clusters, schedule controlled dedicated cluster rebalances to validate, and then deploy to Hosted and Dedicated with monitoring guardrails. Prepare customer-facing incident summary + rollback playbook.

Artifacts: reproduction harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability-harness/compare/feature/wm-inversion, PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/1428, runbook draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/WM-Inversion-Runbook
comments: 2025-02-15 — Initial escalation from Support: Tenant T-998 reported dashboards blanking for 3 distinct routes. Attached sample tenant ID and timeframe. Assigned to Diego.

2025-02-16 — Engineering triage: Leah Kim and Priya Shah validated gaps and provided packet captures. Noted that API ingress shows repeated retries at 10s intervals for a background job which amplified load during rebalance.

2025-02-18 — Reproduction: Asha created a harness to force concurrent leader elections + retries; reproduced missing index segments locally. Added detailed debug logs in shard coordinator (link to logs in Confluence).

2025-02-20 — Temporary mitigation: throttled autoscaler on affected Dedicated region and enabled conservative checkpointing to prevent further tombstoning while root cause investigated; customer-facing status updated.

2025-02-24 — Code changes: Diego opened PR #1428 implementing watermark-max merge logic and compensating backfill. Unit tests added for inverted-watermark scenarios. Performance regression testing passed on staging. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/1428

2025-02-26 — Canary: Rolled hotfix to canary cluster A for 48h. Observed no new tombstone events; dashboards stable. One edge-case where backfill job overlapped with live ingestion — implemented lock to serialize backfill per-shard.
2025-03-01 — QA: Ran end-to-end smoke with synthetic tenants and trace replay. Trace stitcher validated after reindex run. Preparing deployment window for Hosted and Dedicated next week.
2025-03-03 — Post-approval: Product and Support reviewed incident summary and customer communication draft. Release manager signed off for console-2025.03 cut.

Open items: finalize automated detection alert for watermark regressions (metric: shard.watermark.inversion.count), add dashboard widgets to show tombstone vs ingestion divergence, confirm no PB data loss for Private customers with air-gapped VPCs.
